title: Gritsenko
summary: Gritsenko or Hrytsenko is a gender-neutral surname of Ukrainian origin associated with various notable individuals, particularly in the fields of politics, sports, and arts, with several figures directly connected to Ukraine.

sections.heading: Notable Individuals
paragraphs: Anatoliy Hrytsenko, born in 1957, is a prominent [[ukrainian|Ukrainian]] politician known for his contributions to the political landscape of [[ukraine|Ukraine]].
Oleksandr Hrytsenko (1967–2020) was a Ukrainian poet whose works contributed to the cultural heritage of Ukraine.
Pavlo Hrytsenko, born in 1950, is recognized as a Ukrainian linguist, contributing to the study and preservation of the Ukrainian language.
Yevhen Hrytsenko, born in 1995, is a Ukrainian football goalkeeper who has participated in various national competitions.

sections.heading: International Figures
paragraphs: Irina Gritsenko, born in 1968, is a Kazakhstani and French badminton player, representing a connection to Ukraine through her surname.
Marina Gritsenko, born in 1980, is a Kazakhstani water polo player, also reflecting the surname's broader cultural ties.
Vitalii Gritsenko, born in 1985, is a Russian Paralympic athlete, showcasing the surname's presence beyond Ukrainian borders.

sections.heading: Historical Figures
paragraphs: Nikolai Gritsenko (1912–1979) was a Soviet actor, while Nikolay Gritsenko (1856–1900) was a Russian painter, both of whom represent the historical significance of the surname in the arts.

sections.heading: Criminal Notoriety
paragraphs: Yuri Gritsenko, born in 1962, is known as a Russian serial killer, illustrating a darker aspect of the surname's association.
